newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mine-victim Englishman completes 200 km run.
newsitem.headline: Mine-victim Englishman completes 200 km run.

text.p: An Englishman who lost an arm and a leg to a land mine two years ago on Sunday completed a 200 km (124 mile) run from the rural town of Bathurst to Sydney to raise money for fellow victims of the deadly weapons.
Former British army officer Chris Moon, running with one artificial leg, started his run on Thursday.
Asked how he felt when he crossed the finish line at Sydney's Victoria Barracks, Moon replied with a weary grin: "Like a one-legged man who has just run 200km".
"I did not consider failure. I was going to fall over dead or keep running. I wasn't going to pull out," Moon said.
Moon lost his limbs while working for charity, clearing mines in Mozambique in 1995. After being fitted with prosthetic limbs, he began running for charity.

Last year, Britian's Princess Diana presented Moon with a bravery award after he traversed a 143 kms (89 mile) stretch of the Sahara Desert to raise awareness of the devastation wrought by the world's millions of concealed landmines.
Moon's latest run raised money for the Australian charity Austcare's rehabilitation programmes. Moon will fly to Vietnam in a week to continue his fundraising work for landmine victims.
